topic: K1 prove transported-mean root-MSE m^-1/2 plus n^-1/2 for a<1, sqrt(log n/n) at a=1, and n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)} for a>1 when f_S~x^a and f_T stays positive at zero. K2 construct calibrated-OT plus boundary local-polynomial attainment. K3 give fixed-class bias-aware honest intervals. K4 prove matching lower bounds and restrict adaptation to explicit self-similarity. Include the boundary-bump witness and RICOT cardiomyopathy consumer. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The efficient representer f_T/f_S has squared source norm integrating x^-a, finite below one and logarithmic at one. Above one, a height-h^s boundary bump separates the target by h^(s+1) with source divergence n h^(2s+a+1), yielding the proposed nonregular rate; an independent target perturbation gives m^-1/2. Truncated calibration away from zero plus local extrapolation supplies a plausible upper spine. Estimated densities and critical honest coverage remain unchecked. For a<1, the finite representer norm recovers ordinary semiparametric efficiency; at a=1, multiscale truncation should prove the logarithmic lower bound with no hidden polynomial loss. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Jointly control calibration error, density estimation, boundary bias, target empirical noise, and bias-aware normal approximation at a=1 and for data-driven bandwidths. EARLY KILL TEST: In the known-density, known-propensity model, compute the bump divergence and exact upper envelope. Stop if the critical rate is not sqrt(log n/n) or if the above-one upper rate misses n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish the sharp two-sample minimax root-MSE frontier for a transported mean when f_S(x) is asymptotic to x^a and f_T(0)>0, including the exact critical behavior at a=1.

source_refs.claim: RICOT identifies the transport density ratio as the Riesz representer and proves efficient regular inference under suitable rate conditions, but does not give a sharp polynomial boundary-overlap phase diagram.
source_refs.author: Anik Burman, Margaret Gamalo, Promit Ghosal, Prosenjit Kundu

source_refs.claim: Inverse-weighted parameters become irregular when identification requires arbitrarily large weights; the rate depends on relative tail conditions and can be slower than parametric.
source_refs.author: Shakeeb Khan, Elie Tamer

source_refs.claim: Moment estimation under covariate shift has a known-law minimax lower bound and a two-stage likelihood-ratio estimator attaining it only up to a logarithmic factor; the paper does not isolate the polynomial boundary critical point.
source_refs.author: Zhen Zhang, Xin Liu, Shaoli Wang, Jiaye Teng

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest theories stop on different sides of the proposed frontier: RICOT supplies a regular Riesz-calibration theory, Khan-Tamer links unbounded inverse weights to tail-dependent irregularity without the transported two-sample Holder boundary class, and Zhang et al. prove generic covariate-shift moment rates only up to logarithms. Searches for the transported-mean polynomial-boundary exponent and the rate n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)} found no theorem deriving this phase diagram. Direct calculation supports but does not prove it: the source norm of f_T/f_S is proportional to the integral of x^{-a}, a boundary bump of height h^s changes the target by h^{s+1} with source divergence n h^{2s+a+1}, and at a=1 a multiscale rather than two-point lower bound is needed to recover the logarithm while independent target sampling imposes the m^{-1/2} floor.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A matching upper-and-lower minimax theorem giving root-MSE m^{-1/2}+n^{-1/2} for a<1, m^{-1/2}+sqrt(log n/n) at a=1, and m^{-1/2}+n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)} for a>1, with an explicit boundary-bump testing pair and a no-hidden-polynomial-loss critical lower bound.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the transported trial-to-real-world mean, the density-ratio/Riesz object, weak-overlap motivation, and cardiomyopathy use case that the frontier would refine.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Trial and target covariate laws differ -> transport requires the target-to-trial Riesz weight -> weak overlap makes that weight unstable -> determine the exact regular-to-nonregular minimax frontier for the transported mean.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute a modulus of continuity for a linear functional, use it for minimax testing lower bounds, and construct a near-minimax affine recovery rule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The transported mean is a boundary-sensitive linear functional whose observation norm changes at a=1, so its modulus should produce both the nonregular exponent and the critical logarithm.

method_exemplars.technique: Two-stage source-function estimation followed by truncated likelihood-ratio calibration, paired with a minimax testing lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its target is the same kind of regression moment under covariate shift, but the polynomial source depletion permits an exact boundary modulus instead of an up-to-log generic rate.

method_exemplars.technique: Relate inverse-weight tail behavior to irregular convergence rates and rate-adaptive inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the proof logic linking unbounded weights to nonparametric rates that must be sharpened for f_S(x) asymptotic to x^a.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether Riesz-calibrated semi-unbalanced optimal transport, truncated on the overlap interior and augmented by boundary local-polynomial extrapolation, attains the polynomial-overlap transported-mean frontier when the source and target densities are unknown.

source_refs.claim: RICOT removes the nonvanishing bias of uncalibrated entropic OT, estimates the Riesz representer with a growing calibration sieve, and proves regular semiparametric efficiency under suitable rate conditions.
source_refs.author: Anik Burman, Margaret Gamalo, Promit Ghosal, Prosenjit Kundu

source_refs.claim: Polynomial extrapolation preserves the original ATE and gives asymptotic normality under weaker overlap, but it does not analyze the transported two-sample Holder boundary class or Riesz-calibrated OT.
source_refs.author: Shunichiro Orihara, Sho Komukai, Fan Li

source_refs.excerpt: No claim is made for unknown assignment propensities, continuous-covariate weight learning, sieve approximation

open_problems.why_unsolved: The web and proposal-bank evidence meet at the same proof boundary. RICOT's load-bearing global calibration and asymptotic-linear argument presumes enough integrability for its Riesz weight, whereas f_T/f_S behaves like x^{-a} here and ceases to be square-integrable at a=1. The accepted finite-cell transport proposal likewise proves feasible target-cell weight learning but explicitly excludes continuous-covariate weight learning and sieve approximation. Limited-overlap extrapolation exists separately, yet searches for Riesz-calibrated OT combined with a Holder boundary local polynomial found no occupied result. The first changed proof step is therefore the global or multinomial weight-concentration lemma: it must become an interior calibration bound on [h,1] plus a local-polynomial boundary bias and variance argument, jointly controlling density estimation, propensity estimation, target empirical noise, and the critical logarithm.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An oracle inequality and risk or limit theorem for a cross-fitted estimator using RICOT calibration on [h,1] and an order-floor(s) local polynomial on [0,h], proving the three frontier rates uniformly while accounting for estimated f_S, estimated f_T, treatment propensity, and the independent target sample.

writing_exemplar.why: Its estimator narrative and rare-cardiomyopathy application supply the destination problem; the new work would replace its regular-efficiency endpoint with a boundary-aware attainment theorem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sampling-score transport can be unstable -> calibrated OT estimates the Riesz transport weight -> regular efficiency still requires integrable overlap -> splice calibrated transport with boundary extrapolation to attain the nonregular frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Semi-unbalanced entropic OT with exact Riesz calibration, growing sieves, cross-fitted outcome regression, and influence-function variance estimation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the exact donor construction; the first changed proof step is replacing global L2 Riesz control by an interior calibration bound plus a boundary remainder.

method_exemplars.technique: Boundary local-polynomial estimation with an explicit worst-case smoothness-class bias bound and bandwidth chosen for the scalar functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The missing [0,h] contribution is a boundary linear functional, so its bias-variance proof transfers after replacing the regular design by density x^a.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate a sequence of overlap-weighted effects, fit their polynomial path, and extrapolate to the original estimand with asymptotic normality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest limited-overlap extrapolation construction, while a local Holder correction would replace its global polynomial path with the boundary contribution required here.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct fixed-Holder-class bias-aware honest confidence intervals for the transported mean under polynomial boundary overlap, including uniform coverage at a=1 and after prespecified or data-searched truncation bandwidths.

source_refs.claim: Bias-aware critical values yield honest scalar-functional intervals for local-polynomial estimators and near-minimax expected length when the smoothness class is fixed in advance.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesar

source_refs.claim: Under irregular identification and many extreme propensity scores, IPW and doubly robust estimators can have alpha-stable limits and the ordinary nonparametric bootstrap is inconsistent.
source_refs.author: Phillip Heiler, Ekaterina Kazak

source_refs.claim: Selecting among inspected bandwidths invalidates ordinary intervals; an adjusted critical value restores coverage and applies to trimming used to ensure treatment-effect overlap.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesar

open_problems.why_unsolved: The available inference theories isolate different failure modes. Armstrong-Kolesar control worst-case local-polynomial bias for regular regression functionals, Heiler-Kazak handle heavy inverse weights through stable-law resampling rather than smoothness-bounded extrapolation, and bandwidth-snooping corrections assume an approximately Gaussian studentized process. The literature scan found no result combining these ingredients for a transported two-sample functional whose variance grows logarithmically at a=1. The unresolved proof is a uniform normal approximation for the sum of the interior calibrated-weight process, the boundary local-polynomial process, and independent target-sample noise when worst-case bias is of standard-error order and the bandwidth may be selected from a grid.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform-coverage and expected-length theorem for an explicit bias-aware interval over a fixed Holder ball, with critical values covering a<1, a=1, and a>1 and a valid multiscale correction for a prespecified bandwidth-search range.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the clean scalar-functional motivation: smoothing is necessary, smoothing creates non-negligible bias, and honest inference must incorporate a class-wide bias bound.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A local-polynomial estimator regularizes a nonparametric functional -> regularization bias can match sampling uncertainty -> conventional Gaussian intervals undercover -> use a fixed-class worst-case bias bound for honest transported-mean inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Fold the exact worst-case smoothing bias into a noncentral-normal critical value and optimize the bandwidth for honest interval length.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The boundary correction is a local-polynomial linear estimator, and the desired resolution is a uniform-coverage statement rather than pointwise asymptotic normality.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian-process supremum critical values indexed by bandwidth to obtain coverage uniform over the searched bandwidth range.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It addresses the exact extra randomness introduced when the truncation and boundary bandwidth is selected after inspecting several scales.

method_exemplars.technique: Develop tail-sensitive stable limit theory and an adaptive m-out-of-n bootstrap under irregular inverse weighting.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It identifies why an ordinary influence-function bootstrap can fail under weak overlap, giving the diagnostic alternative the boundary-smoothing Gaussian proof must dominate or exclude.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize when honest transported-mean intervals can adapt to unknown boundary smoothness s, or jointly to s and overlap exponent a, and whether an explicit boundary self-similarity condition is necessary and sufficient for rate adaptation.

source_refs.claim: For confidence intervals on linear functionals, a between-class modulus determines adaptive expected length and yields sharp lower bounds and near-optimal constructions.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai, Mark G. Low

source_refs.claim: Honest adaptive confidence bands generally require a smaller function class, and self-similarity is necessary and sufficient in the Holder settings studied there.
source_refs.author: Adam D. Bull

source_refs.claim: Honest scalar-functional intervals are built over fixed smoothness classes; the framework explains why unrestricted data-driven smoothness calibration requires additional restrictions.
source_refs.author: Timothy B. Armstrong, Michal Kolesar

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cai-Low gives the abstract adaptive-confidence-interval modulus for linear functionals, Bull supplies self-similarity results for function bands, and Armstrong-Kolesar supplies the fixed-class scalar-functional benchmark. None specializes those arguments to a transported functional whose observation norm changes at a=1 and whose target sample adds an m^{-1/2} floor. The missing mathematical object is the between-class modulus under source design density x^a: it must determine whether adaptation across the regular/nonregular boundary is impossible and whether a boundary-local self-similarity restriction makes the relevant bias observable without assuming the desired rate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A paired impossibility-and-attainment characterization proving nonadaptation of honest interval length over unrestricted unions of (s,a)-classes and constructing a multiscale honest interval with class-optimal length under an explicit boundary self-similarity condition.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames adaptation directly for confidence intervals on scalar linear functionals, closer to a transported mean than function-band treatments.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A scalar linear functional has class-dependent minimax difficulty -> honest coverage couples easy and hard classes through a between-class modulus -> unrestricted adaptation may be impossible -> characterize the extra restriction permitting adaptive transported-mean intervals.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute ordered and between-class moduli of continuity to derive expected-length lower bounds and construct adaptive confidence intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested resolution is exactly an adaptive confidence-interval characterization for a linear functional, with the transported design changing the modulus.

method_exemplars.technique: Use multiscale persistence under self-similarity to construct honest adaptive confidence bands and prove the restriction is necessary in the studied Holder models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Boundary bumps are the least-favorable alternatives here, so persistence of boundary signal across scales is the natural analogue of Bull's self-similarity mechanism.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct fixed-class bias-aware intervals and optimize bandwidth for interval length over a convex smoothness class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives the scalar local-polynomial interval that a self-similar adaptive construction must select among without losing honesty.

literature_map:
1. RICOT (Burman, Gamalo, Ghosal, Kundu, 2026, arXiv:2608.23453) is the exact estimator and application anchor: Riesz calibration, semi-unbalanced entropic OT, regular efficiency, and rare progressive cardiomyopathy.
2. Khan-Tamer (2010, Econometrica, 10.3982/ECTA7372) establishes that inverse-weight identification can be irregular and its rate is governed by tail and support behavior.
3. Hong-Leung-Li (2020, Econometrics Journal, 10.1093/ectj/utz017) derives slower convergence under degenerating overlap in a finite-population asymptotic regime.
4. Ma-Wang (2020, JASA, 10.1080/01621459.2019.1660173) distinguishes Gaussian and non-Gaussian IPW limits and studies bias-corrected trimming.
5. Heiler-Kazak (2021, Journal of Econometrics, 10.1016/j.jeconom.2020.03.025) obtains alpha-stable limits and adaptive m-out-of-n bootstrap inference without strong support restrictions.
6. Sasaki-Ura (2022, Econometric Theory, 10.1017/S0266466621000025) debiases trimmed ratio moments by polynomial regression near a small denominator.
7. Chaudhuri-Hill (2025, Econometric Reviews, 10.1080/07474938.2024.2444229) trims the heavy-tailed IPW variable itself and estimates asymmetric trimming bias.
8. Zhang-Liu-Wang-Teng (2025, ICLR, arXiv:2506.23453) gives generic minimax covariate-shift moment estimation, known-law lower bounds, and truncated doubly robust upper bounds only up to logs.
9. Orihara-Komukai-Li (2026, arXiv:2608.09329) extrapolates a polynomial path of overlap-weighted effects to the ATE under weaker overlap, but does not treat the transported Holder boundary problem.
10. Josey-Berkowitz-Ghosh-Raghavan (2021, Statistics in Medicine, 10.1002/sim.9031) supplies doubly robust entropy-balancing transport under regular positivity.
11. Chen-Chen-Yu (2023, Biometrics, 10.1111/biom.13825) develops entropy balancing from target summary moments and exposes limits on target-population variance evaluation with summary information.
12. Armstrong-Kolesar (2020, Quantitative Economics, 10.3982/QE1199) supplies fixed-class honest local-polynomial intervals based on explicit worst-case bias.
13. Armstrong-Kolesar (2018, Review of Economic Studies, 10.1093/restud/rdx051) corrects bandwidth snooping and explicitly applies the correction to overlap trimming.
14. Cai-Low (2004, Annals of Statistics, 10.1214/009053604000000049) characterizes adaptive interval length for linear functionals through between-class moduli.
15. Bull (2012, Electronic Journal of Statistics, 10.1214/12-EJS720) proves self-similarity necessary and sufficient for honest adaptive bands in its Holder settings.
